facts.text: Fort Hamilton was officially named in the twentieth century for Alexander Hamilton, the first Secretary of the Treasury.
The cornerstone for Fort Hamilton was set in 1825 by Simon Bernard, a former military engineer under Napoleon.
Fort Hamilton was designed as a trapezoid with two tiers of cannons to defend the Narrows from sea and land attacks.
A rare feature called a caponier projects into the dry ditch to defend the landward sides of Fort Hamilton.
The original fort was completed in 1831 and is part of the third system of United States seacoast forts.
Fort Hamilton now serves as a military installation supporting the Army National Guard and the United States Army Reserve.
